However, the benefits of using Git branches and tags, such as being able to work on multiple features independently and marking specific points in your repository's history, outweigh the costs.

#9730. Is a gas oven bad for bread?: Why a gas oven may be interfering with your go-to steaming method.

Adapted from King Arthur Baking Company’s Big Book of Bread

One of the most crucial steps for making crusty artisan-style bread comes at the very end: steaming.

Baking bread with steam is critical for achieving expansive, open-crumbed loaves with a golden, crisp crust. If you bake bread in a dry oven, the crust quickly sets, which prevents the dough from expanding to its full potential; this, in turn, leads to loaves with a denser crumb. If you introduce steam at the start of the bake, the crust remains moist and pliable and the loaf can stretch and expand before the crust sets, resulting in a lighter, more open crumb.

What’s more, steam also helps gelatinize starches on the loaf’s exterior, which helps it brown and creates an especially crispy, flavorful, and shiny loaf. (Learn more: A guide to baking bread with steam at home.)

There are many different ways to steam your bread, all of which are designed to introduce moisture to the oven during the first part of baking. The most common method involves setting a large cast-iron skillet below your baking stone or steel when you preheat the oven. After you load your bread into the oven, you immediately pour a cup or so of warm water into the preheated cast-iron skillet and quickly close the door so the steam doesn’t escape.

This method works great, with one exception: It’s not effective in a gas oven.

If you have a gas oven, it’s very hard to add sufficient steam. By design, gas ovens vent out effluence, meaning whatever steam you add is very quickly vented out of the oven chamber. This is particularly true if you steam your bread by pouring hot water into a cast-iron skillet, as outlined above. All the water quickly dissipates, and there’s not enough moisture left to enhance the crust.

But all is not lost. There is a workaround.

If you’re steaming bread in a gas oven, you need to use a preheated covered baker, such as a Dutch oven. Instead of adding an additional water source, the lidded vessel traps the steam that escapes from the loaf as it bakes, becoming a kind of self-steaming oven. Because the steam is sealed in, the gas oven won’t vent it out.

You can use a Dutch oven for a round, boule-shaped loaf, or any other form of covered baker, like the Brod & Taylor Bread Steel for elongated, bâtard-shaped loaves. (There’s also a round version of the Bread Steel available.)

For more guidance on this method, see our previous blogs, Bread baking in a Dutch oven and For crispy, crackle crusts, put a lid on it.

When you load your dough into the oven, slip a few ice cubes between the parchment beneath your loaf and the pan to give the loaf an extra initial burst of steam. Just don’t skip the parchment beneath the dough. Otherwise, the extra water from the melting ice may cause your bread to stick to the pot.

#9729. Build an HTCondor Pool on Ubuntu and Run Your First Remote Job

Part 1 of 6 in Building and Operating an HTCondor Pool for Research Computing.

Suppose you have one training run per participant in a study and several workstations that could run them. With HTCondor, you can submit each run as a job and specify the CPU, memory, and GPU it needs. The workstations advertise what they can offer. HTCondor keeps each job in a queue until it can match it to a suitable machine. The machines that cooperate this way form a pool.

I administer the central manager for our lab’s pool. Our November 2026 inventory lists twelve machines. The workstation that hosts the central manager also accepts submissions and runs jobs. Some of the other workstations only run jobs, while others also accept submissions.

For this walkthrough, we’ll put each role on a separate Ubuntu 24.04 VM. You’ll submit a shell script and a text file from the access point (the submit node). The script will run on the worker and print its hostname and a line from the file. You’ll read both lines back on the access point.

Start with three fresh VMs on a private network. Each needs Bash, curl, sudo, and access to the Ubuntu and HTCondor package repositories. Run uname -m on the access point and worker and check that the results match. The submit file below uses HTCondor’s default architecture requirement, which matches the architecture of the access point even when the executable is a shell script.

Allow TCP port 9618 between pool members. Before installing, check name resolution on each host. Substitute your own hostnames below and confirm that each resolves to its intended private address.

Start on the manager, then install the access point, then the worker. Enter the same pool password on all three. On each host, the installer uses that shared secret to generate a daemon token. The daemons use these tokens to authenticate to one another with HTCondor’s IDTOKENS method. Researchers submit jobs from their own local accounts on the access point.

On each host, download the installer into your home directory. Set manager to the same real manager name everywhere. In a Bash shell on each host, first run the one assignment from its row, then run the common commands below. The installer takes the manager’s name even on the worker.

The dry run shows the proposed installation commands. The 25.0 channel selects the HTCondor 25.0 LTS release series. Once the role and manager name look right, run the following in the same Bash session on that host. The silent prompt keeps the pool password out of your typed command history. The installer reads it from standard input.

After the installer succeeds on each machine, check the installed version, the manager it points to, and the local service:

Once the manager’s service is active, test its TCP port from both the access point and the worker. Use the manager variable you set on each host. On Ubuntu, nc is available in the netcat-openbsd package (sudo apt install netcat-openbsd if needed).

If the connection times out or is refused, check the manager’s service, the resolved address, and the firewall rules. A successful connection establishes TCP reachability. To check whether the daemons have also registered with the collector, run the following on the access point after all three services have started. Allow time for their first advertisements.

For this layout, look for all three hosts in the first query, the access point in the second, and at least one slot on the worker in the third. A master entry tells you that the host’s managing daemon advertised itself. The slot entry tells you what that worker is offering. A machine can appear in the first list while offering no slots.

Log in to the access point as a regular user. Create a working directory. Put a short script and a text file in it:

In that directory, save this as first.sub. HTCondor will transfer the executable and the specified input file, so the worker can run the test without a shared home directory, NAS mount, or Python environment.

Submit the job and note the cluster number printed by condor_submit. A quick job may already have finished by the time you inspect the queue.

Set cluster to the number printed at submission. The submit file queues one process, so its job ID ends in .0. Wait up to three minutes for a completion or removal event.

If the wait times out or reports an error, use the troubleshooting steps below. A zero exit status from condor_wait can also mean the job was removed. Check the job’s own exit status and read its standard output on the access point.

For a successful run, expect 4 false 0 in the history. These values mean the job completed, exited normally, and returned exit code zero. The output file should look like this.

The first line should match the output of hostname on your worker. The second shows that the script read the transferred file. Reading both lines on the access point confirms that stdout made the return trip.

If the wait times out, the job may still be queued or running. On the access point, check its state and recent events.

JobStatus 1 means Idle, 2 means Running, and 5 means Held. For a running job, repeat the wait with the same ID. If the queue query returns no row, check the history again. If the event log is missing, check the cluster number and make sure you are in ~/first-condor-job.

For workstations joining our existing lab pool, I issue the daemon token centrally. A colleague sends me the workstation’s network address. I create the token on the central manager with condor_token_create and give it to the colleague. They configure the workstation with our manager and trust domain and install the token under /etc/condor/tokens.d/ with restricted permissions.

Our central manager is configured with use ROLE : CentralManager, Submit, Execute. For a workstation that will both accept submissions and run jobs, our setup instructions specify use ROLE : Submit, Execute. I look for its schedd with condor_status -schedd and its execution slots with condor_status. Submitting a job from the colleague’s local account checks that the workstation’s schedd accepts jobs from that user. To see which workstation actually ran the job, check the hostname printed by the probe.

People also use these workstations at their desks. Our setup instructions use START = (Cpus > 0) && (LoadAvg / Cpus < 0.4) to decide when a slot can accept a new job. A workstation can remain visible in the pool while this condition prevents a new job from starting. On a partitionable slot, Cpus counts the CPUs still available. As jobs claim CPUs, the denominator gets smaller, so even an unchanged LoadAvg can bring the ratio up to the cutoff.

After the CPU test succeeds, you can configure HTCondor to let two jobs share one NVIDIA GPU. On the idle worker, check that nvidia-smi -L lists the expected card, then apply the settings below.

-divide 2 makes condor_gpu_discovery list the same device ID twice in DetectedGPUs and report half its usual GlobalMemoryMb value for matching. Two jobs that each request one GPU can therefore be assigned the same card. They share its VRAM, and either job can use more than the advertised half if enough memory is free. Once the worker advertises again, run condor_status -gpus on the access point to inspect the pool’s GPU resources.

#9728. TOP 11 AI MARKETING TOOLS YOU SHOULD USE (Updated 2022)

If you’re late to the AI party, don’t worry. It’s easier than you think to start leveraging artificial intelligence tools in your marketing strategy. Here are 11 AI marketing tools every marketer should start using today.

Personalize is an AI-powered technology that helps you identify and produce highly targeted sales and marketing campaigns by tracking the products and services your contacts are most interested in at any given time. The platform uses an algorithm to identify each contact’s top three interests, which are updated in real-time based on recent site activity.

Seventh Sense provides behavioral analytics that helps you win attention in your customers’ overcrowded email inboxes. Choosing the best day and time to send an email is always a gamble. And while some days of the week generally get higher open rates than others, you’ll never be able to nail down a time that’s best for every customer. Seventh Sense eases your stress of having to figure out the perfect send-time and day for your email campaigns. The AI-based platform figures out the best timing and email frequency for each contact based on when they’re opening emails. The tool is primarily geared toward HubSpot and Marketo customers

Phrasee uses artificial intelligence to help you write more effective subject lines. With its AI-based Natural Language Generation system, Phrasee uses data-driven insights to generate millions of natural-sounding copy variants that match your brand voice. The model is end-to-end, meaning when you feed the results back to Phrasee, the prediction model rebuilds so it can continuously learn from your audience.

HubSpot Search Engine Optimization (SEO) is an integral tool for the Human Content team. It uses machine learning to determine how search engines understand and categorize your content. HubSpot SEO helps you improve your search engine rankings and outrank your competitors. Search engines reward websites that organize their content around core subjects, or topic clusters. HubSpot SEO helps you discover and rank for the topics that matter to your business and customers.

When you’re limited to testing two variables against each other at a time, it can take months to get the results you’re looking for. Evolv AI lets you test all your ideas at once. It uses advanced algorithms to identify the top-performing concepts, combine them with each other, and repeat the process to achieve the best site experience.

Acrolinx is a content alignment platform that helps brands scale and improves the quality of their content. It’s geared toward enterprises – its major customers include big brands like Google, Adobe, and Amazon - to help them scale their writing efforts. Instead of spending time chasing down and fixing typos in multiple places throughout an article or blog post, you can use Acrolinx to do it all right there in one place. You start by setting your preferences for style, grammar, tone of voice, and company-specific word usage. Then, Acrolinx checks and scores your existing content to find what’s working and suggest areas for improvement. The platform provides real-time guidance and suggestions to make writing better and strengthen weak pages.

MarketMuse uses an algorithm to help marketers build content strategies. The tool shows you where to target keywords to rank in specific topic categories, and recommends keywords you should go after if you want to own particular topics. It also identifies gaps and opportunities for new content and prioritizes them by their probable impact on your rankings. The algorithm compares your content with thousands of articles related to the same topic to uncover what’s missing from your site.

Copilot is a suite of tools that help eCommerce businesses maintain real-time communication with customers around the clock at every stage of the funnel. Promote products, recover shopping carts and send updates or reminders directly through Messenger.

Yotpo’s deep learning technology evaluates your customers’ product reviews to help you make better business decisions. It identifies key topics that customers mention related to your products—and their feelings toward them. The AI engine extracts relevant reviews from past buyers and presents them in smart displays to convert new shoppers. Yotpo also saves you time moderating reviews. The AI-powered moderation tool automatically assigns a score to each review and flags reviews with negative sentiment so you can focus on quality control instead of manually reviewing every post.

Albert is a self-learning software that automates the creation of marketing campaigns for your brand. It analyzes vast amounts of data to run optimized campaigns autonomously, allowing you to feed in your own creative content and target markets, and then use data from its database to determine key characteristics of a serious buyer. Albert identifies potential customers that match those traits, and runs trial campaigns on a small group of customers—with results refined by Albert himself—before launching it on a larger scale.

Albert plugs into your existing marketing technology stack, so you still have access to your accounts, ads, search, social media, and more. Albert maps tracking and attribution to your source of truth so you can determine which channels are driving your business.

There are many tools and companies out there that offer AI tools, but this is a small list of resources that we have found to be helpful. If you have any other suggestions, feel free to share them in the comments below this article. As marketing evolves at such a rapid pace, new marketing strategies will be invented that we haven't even dreamed of yet. But for now, this list should give you a good starting point on your way to implementing AI into your marketing mix.

Say you are a mobile developer tasked with optimizing the offline-first sync functionality of your React Native application. Your users are complaining about slow sync times, and you suspect that the current implementation is not efficient. However, before embarking on a potentially costly rewrite, you want to understand the current performance characteristics of your sync mechanism. You've tried using the application on a slow network, but it's difficult to quantify the issues and prioritize optimizations.

Offline-first sync is a complex problem, involving caching, conflict resolution, and network communication. On mobile devices, additional constraints such as limited storage, processing power, and network bandwidth come into play. Without proper instrumentation, it's challenging to identify the bottlenecks in the sync pipeline. The symptoms of poor performance can be misleading, and optimizing the wrong components can lead to wasted effort and even introduce new issues.

To measure the performance of your offline-first sync, follow these steps:

Instrumenting your sync pipeline and collecting performance data will incur some overhead in terms of development time and resources. However, this investment is crucial to ensure that any optimization efforts are targeted and effective. If your application's sync performance is not a major concern, or if you have limited resources, you may need to prioritize other features or bug fixes. Additionally, if your application's sync mechanism is relatively simple, the benefits of instrumentation may not outweigh the costs.

When interviewing a candidate for a mobile development position, you may ask a question like: "How would you approach optimizing the offline-first sync performance of a React Native application?" A weak answer might focus on general optimization techniques without considering the specific challenges of offline-first sync. #9725. Building a Sticky Mobile Call Bar for a Law Firm Website

Most visitors to a criminal defense website arrive on a phone, and many of them want to call rather than read. A sticky call bar, a strip pinned to the bottom of the screen with a tap-to-call button, is one of the most common patterns on law firm sites for that reason. It is also one of the most commonly broken. Bars cover footer links, collide with chat widgets, sit under the iPhone home indicator or hide the last line of every page.

This post walks through building one that behaves well: correct on notched phones, accessible, easy to measure and out of the way of the content. The examples use plain HTML and CSS with a few lines of JavaScript, so they port to any CMS or framework.

Keep the bar simple. One primary action, the phone call, and at most one secondary action, such as a link to the contact form. Two buttons fit comfortably on small screens. Three usually do not.

Use a real tel: link with the number in international format, and put the human-readable number in the visible text. Screen reader users and people who distrust buttons both benefit from seeing the actual number. Wrap the bar in a landmark element with a label so assistive technology can identify it.

On phones with a home indicator, content at the very bottom of the viewport can sit underneath it. CSS environment variables solve this, but only if the viewport meta tag opts in with viewport-fit=cover. Without that, env(safe-area-inset-bottom) returns zero and the bar may be partly covered.

The body padding matters. Without it, the bar covers the last part of every page, which on a law firm site is often the footer with the disclaimer and office addresses. Match the padding to the bar's real height, and test with large text settings, since the bar grows when the user increases the font size.

WCAG 2.2 added a target size criterion at level AA that sets a minimum of 24 by 24 CSS pixels for most targets, with some exceptions. That is a floor. For the main call button on a defense site, aim much larger, around 44 to 48 pixels tall, since the person tapping it may be stressed, in a car or using one hand.

Check contrast too. A white phone number on a pale brand color may look fine in a design file and fail outdoors on a phone. Run the colors through a contrast checker and aim for at least the AA ratio for normal text.

Decide on a stacking order and stick to it. Common choices are to move the chat launcher above the bar with a bottom offset, or to fold chat into the bar as the secondary action. Hide the bar while the on-screen keyboard is open on form pages, since it can cover the field the user is typing in. Listening for focus on inputs and toggling a class works on most devices.

A call bar on every page is the default, but it is worth reconsidering. On a long charge page, the bar keeps the number in reach. On the contact page, which already shows the number and a form, it adds clutter. On a printable page, such as courthouse directions, hide it in a print stylesheet.

Some sites reveal the bar only after the visitor scrolls past the first screen, so the hero section stays clean. That can work, but test it. A visitor who wants to call immediately should not have to scroll to find the number.

Content matters as much as code. The words on the button affect whether people tap it, and plain labels such as "Call now" next to the actual number tend to be clearer than vague promises. This article on writing the words around the call button on a defense site covers the copy side.

Track taps on the call link as an event in your analytics tool. Attach the listener to the link and do not prevent the default action, so the dialer still opens if the analytics script is slow or blocked. Record which page the tap came from, since that is the data the marketing side will ask for.

Remember that a tap is not a call. Some users tap and hang up before connecting. If the firm uses a call tracking service, compare tap events with connected calls by page every month to see how far the numbers drift apart.

Emulators catch layout problems, but they miss the details that matter here: the home indicator, the dynamic toolbar in mobile browsers that changes the viewport height while scrolling, and how the bar behaves when the keyboard opens. Test on at least one recent iPhone and one Android phone, held upright and turned sideways, with the system font size turned up.

For more on design for defense firm websites, the law firm website design guides cover layout, typography and mobile patterns.

A small bar that does not cover the main content is generally fine. Avoid anything that hides most of the screen on page load, since intrusive overlays can create a poor experience on mobile.

Usually not. Desktop visitors rarely place calls from the browser, and a header with the phone number serves them better.

Yes, with an sms: link, if the firm actually monitors that number. Make sure someone replies quickly and that texting fits the firm's intake rules.

SBD Marketing works only with criminal defense firms, one per city. It designs and builds websites for defense practices, handles SEO for the charges they defend, runs SEO audits and works on visibility in AI search tools.

#9721. This fall, reach for this unlikely apple ingredient : Apple cider vinegar is a baker’s secret weapon.

As fall baking season settles in, you're probably reaching for apples — and the many flavor-packed ingredients they produce. Applesauce cooks down into tangy apple butter to be cradled in a flaky galette, while a drop of boiled cider can deliver supercharged apple flavor to crumb cake. But the baking ingredient you may be overlooking may be something you associate more with salad dressings and wellness tonics: apple cider vinegar.

This tangy, apple-y vinegar is a secret ingredient in some of our favorite fall recipes, including cookbook author Claire Saffitz’s Cinnamon-and-Sugar Apple Pie. While lemon juice is the standard acid used in most fruit pie fillings, Claire opts for apple cider vinegar here to complement the filling’s flavors. “It helps as a flavor enhancer, and I also like that it’s apple cider in an apple pie. It’s a nice symmetry,” she mentions.

Similarly, apple cider vinegar is used in the cooking liquid alongside sugar and butter to caramelize apples in a Classic Apple Tarte Tatin. The benefit is twofold: Vinegar’s acidity helps cut the sweetness of the caramel, and it prevents the apples from getting too mushy, instead maintaining their fork-tender texture.

Pastry chef and cookbook author Natasha Pickowicz often leans into the jolt vinegar can add, including adding a few drops to her cake soaks for an additional layer of flavor. “Cake soaks should have a balance of tart, sweet, and savory notes — just like vinaigrette for your favorite salad,” she writes in her cookbook More Than Cake. It can add intrigue to layered cakes like this Golden Spice Cake or Pumpkin Layer Cake. In her cookbook, she also calls for a glaze spiked with apple cider vinegar to brush onto an apple tart after baking. It’s the finishing touch “to further emphasize the tart’s resolute apple-ness,” she writes.

Apple cider vinegar doesn’t need to be limited to only apple desserts, either. In our Old-Fashioned Pecan Pie, we call for apple cider vinegar as a foil to the brown sugar filling’s cloying sweetness. A spoonful of apple cider vinegar may not announce itself boldly, but it makes a small splash for brighter, more balanced bakes.

#9713. What is high-extraction flour, exactly?  : A baker’s guide to our new T85 Baker's Reserve Bread Flour.

High-extraction flour is a technical term that often prompts a lot of confusion from those unfamiliar with it. But with the debut of our new high-extraction flour, known as Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour, we’re breaking down just what it is and why it's a great choice for avid bread makers.

The extraction rate of a flour refers to how much of the original grain — the bran, germ, and endosperm — ends up in the final flour. A high-extraction flour typically has an extraction rate of about 80% to 90%, meaning some of the bran and germ have been sifted out, but it still retains much of the original grain. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning its extraction rate is 85%.

To put that in perspective, whole wheat flour has an extraction rate of 100%; it retains the entirety of the grain, including the bran, germ, and endosperm.

High-extraction flour falls between white and whole wheat flour. It’s lighter and less coarse than whole wheat flour because some of the bran has been sifted out, but it still retains more flavor, nutrients, and color than white flour, since it retains much of the original grain.

High-extraction flour is popular for artisan bread baking because it offers a balance of nutrition and good gluten development. It’s great for rustic loaves, baguettes, and pizza dough, and particularly well-suited for sourdough baking because it strikes a balance between flavor, nutrition, fermentation, and dough strength.

You can substitute our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour 1:1 for bread flour (by weight or volume) in artisanal bread recipes; it can also be used 1:1 to replace the total flour in recipes that call for a combination of all-purpose and whole wheat flour. If you're subbing Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour for all-purpose flour in a bread recipe, you may find you need to add slightly more liquid to the recipe.

Bread bakers love high-extraction flour for artisan bread and sourdough because it offers the flavor and nutrition of whole grain flour; the stronger gluten development and more open crumb you get from white flour; and better fermentation from the minerals present in the bran and germ, which feed the wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria in sourdough starter, promoting more active fermentation.

If you want a loaf of bread that’s more flavorful and nutritious than bread made with exclusively white flour, but that still rises high and has an open crumb, high-extraction flour is a great choice.

Yes — in fact, it’s a great choice for feeding starter because of the sourdough-friendly minerals present in the flour, which boost activity in your starter.

Yes! T85 is a French specification that refers to the extraction rate (85%) of the flour. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning the extraction rate is 85%. If you have a recipe that calls for T85, this flour is the perfect choice.

Find our high-extraction Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour online.

#9708. Top 10 AI Tools in 2023 That Will Make Your Life Easier

In this article, we explore the top 10 AI tools that are driving innovation and efficiency in various industries. These tools are designed to automate repetitive tasks, improve workflow, and increase productivity. The tools included in our list are some of the most advanced and widely used in the market, and are suitable for a variety of applications. Some of the tools focus on natural language processing, such as ChatGPT and Grammarly, while others focus on image and video generation, such as DALL-E and Lumen5. Other tools such as OpenAI Codex, Tabnine, Canva, Jasper AI,, and Surfer SEO are designed to help with specific tasks such as code understanding content writing and website optimization. This list is a great starting point for anyone looking to explore the possibilities of AI and how it can be applied to their business or project.

ChatGPT is a large language model that generates human-like responses to a variety of prompts. It can be used for tasks such as language translation, question answering, and text completion. It can handle a wide range of topics and styles of writing, and generates coherent and fluent text, but should be used with care as it may generate text that is biased, offensive, or factually incorrect.

Overall, ChatGPT is a powerful tool for natural language processing, but it should be used with care and with an understanding of its limitations.

DALL-E is a generative model developed by OpenAI that is capable of generating images from text prompts. It is based on the GPT-3 architecture, which is a transformer-based neural network language model that has been trained on a massive dataset of text. DALL-E can generate images that are similar to a training dataset and it can generate high-resolution images that are suitable for commercial use.

Overall, DALL-E is a powerful AI-based tool for generating images, it can be used for a variety of applications such as creating images for commercial use, gaming, and other creative projects. It is important to note that the generated images should be reviewed and used with care, as they may not be entirely original and could be influenced by the training data.

Lumen5 is a content creation platform that uses AI to help users create videos, social media posts, and other types of content. It has several features that make it useful for content creation and marketing, including:

Overall, Lumen5 is a useful tool for creating content quickly and easily, it can help automate the process of creating videos, social media posts, and other types of content. However, the quality of the generated content may vary depending on the source material and it is important to review and edit the content before publishing it.

Grammarly is a writing-enhancement platform that uses AI to check for grammar, punctuation, and spelling errors in the text. It also provides suggestions for improving the clarity, concision, and readability of the text. It has several features that make it useful for improving writing, including:

OpenAI Codex is a system developed by OpenAI that can create code from natural language descriptions of software tasks. The system is based on the GPT-3 model and can generate code in multiple programming languages.

Overall, OpenAI Codex is a powerful tool that can help automate the process of writing code and make it more accessible to non-technical people. However, the quality of the generated code may vary depending on the task description and it is important to review and test the code before using it in a production environment. It is important to use the tool as an aid, not a replacement for the developer's knowledge.

Tabnine is a code completion tool that uses AI to predict and suggest code snippets. It is compatible with multiple programming languages and can be integrated with various code editors.

Overall, TabNine is a useful tool for developers that can help improve coding efficiency and reduce the time spent on writing code. However, it is important to review the suggestions provided by the tool and use them with caution, as they may not always be accurate or appropriate. It is important to use the tool as an aid, not a replacement for the developer's knowledge.

Jasper is a content writing and content generation tool that uses artificial intelligence to identify the best words and sentences for your writing style and medium in the most efficient, quick, and accessible way.

Overall, Surfer SEO can be a useful tool for website owners and digital marketers looking to improve their SEO efforts. However, it is important to remember that it is just a tool and should be used in conjunction with other SEO best practices. Additionally, the tool is not a guarantee of better ranking.

Zapier is a web automation tool that allows users to automate repetitive tasks by connecting different web applications together. It does this by creating "Zaps" that automatically move data between apps, and can also be used to trigger certain actions in one app based on events in another app.

Overall, Zapier is a useful tool that can help users automate repetitive tasks and improve workflow. It can save time and increase productivity by connecting different web applications together. However, it may require some technical skills and some features may require a paid subscription. It is important to use the tool with caution and not to rely too much on it, to understand the apps better.

Compose AI is a company that specializes in developing natural language generation (NLG) software. Their software uses AI to automatically generate written or spoken text from structured data, such as spreadsheets, databases, or APIs.

Overall, Compose AI's NLG software can be a useful tool for automating the process of creating written or spoken content from structured data. However, the quality of the generated content may vary depending on the data source, and it is essential to review the generated content before using it in a production environment. But when we do get the chance, we want a slam-dunk recipe — or 12. Here’s a dozen of the favorite fall recipes we’ll be making this month: from pumpkin cake bars to spooky fudge brownies to a crowd-pleasing vegetarian quiche.

It’s the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown! Only this version comes in cake form. The decoration is deceptively easy: Stack two small Bundts, frost the entire thing, and add a chocolate-dipped ice cream cone for the stem.

Get the recipe: The Great Pumpkin Bundt Cake

To make this recipe, you’ll need: Boiled Cider and Apple Pie Spice

If you like this recipe, you may also like: Apple Pie Bars, Tiny Apple Tarts for Two

Step aside, soup: Butternut squash truly shines in this autumnal quiche. Caramelized onions finished with balsamic vinegar and fresh baby spinach round out the filling, while our Classic Single Pie Crust recipe ensures a tender, golden crust. Elevate the edges with the pie crust decorating technique of your choice.

Ready to test the theory that only white flour can make rolls light and fluffy? "Tassie" means "small cup" in Scottish, and these dainty pecan pies pack a nutty punch. The cream cheese pastry crust is cut into rounds and placed in a mini muffin pan before the pecan pie filling is spooned into each well. With only 30 minutes of hands-on time, these two dozen tassies come together quickly on a crisp fall afternoon.

To make this recipe, you’ll need: Mini Muffin Pan

If you like this recipe, you may also like: Easy Pecan Pie Bars, Old-Fashioned Pecan Pie

Need a spooky treat, stat? You can transform a plain batch of brownies into a Halloween-themed dessert in a pinch. A simple piping technique creates a spider web effect and adds a touch of rich tang to chocolatey brownies.
